temario.subtitulo: What you study and how you study it.
temario.vacio: No topics yet. Add the syllabus and FOCUS spreads it out until the exam.
temario.archivarCuerpo: It stops showing in FOCUS. Its hours and grades stay in your data.

examenes.mediaGlobal: Average of your subjects, out of 10.

mision.explica: If you finish the whole block and reach the minutes it asks for, the mission checks itself off. The block gives no XP on its own.

noMolestar.honesto: NIVL can't silence your phone or block other apps: only your phone can do that. Turn it on yourself before you start, it takes two taps.

ios.0: Swipe down from the top right corner to open Control Center.
ios.1: Tap Focus and choose Do Not Disturb (or create a “Study” focus).
ios.2: When the block ends, turn it off the same way. The NIVL alert reaches you if you allow it in that focus.

android.0: Swipe down twice from the top to open quick settings.
android.1: Tap Do Not Disturb (or Focus mode, depending on the maker).
android.2: When the block ends, turn it off the same way. Let NIVL alerts through if you want to hear the end.

noMolestar.consejo: Even better: phone face down and out of reach. What you can't see doesn't call you.
noMolestar.guiadoRotulo: Really lock yourself in on iPhone
noMolestar.guiadoCuerpo: Guided Access keeps the iPhone inside NIVL until you turn it off. It comes with iOS, not NIVL.

guiado.0: In Settings, Accessibility, turn on Guided Access and set a passcode.
guiado.1: Open NIVL, press the side button three times and tap Start.
guiado.2: To leave, three more presses and your passcode.

ajustes.encadenarAyuda: When focus ends the break starts on its own, and the other way round.
ajustes.sinClasesAyuda: During exam season the plan doesn't wait for classes to end. Day and month: 20/1.

recuerdo.linea: Pull it from memory, don't reread it.
recuerdo.que: Studying is retrieving, not rereading. You close your notes and force yourself to bring out what you know.

pasos.0: Read a section only once, carefully.
pasos.1: Close your notes and write or say everything you remember.
pasos.2: Open them and compare: mark what was missing or wrong.
pasos.3: Repeat only what you missed until you get it all out.

recuerdo.porQue: Every time you retrieve something from memory, the memory gets stronger than it does by rereading. It is one of the most studied findings in the psychology of learning.

espaciada.que: Review right when you start to forget. FOCUS puts each topic and each card on its day.

pasos.0: Study the topic and mark it as reviewing.
pasos.1: Tomorrow it shows up in Today's reviews: review it from memory.
pasos.2: If you knew it, the next review moves further away (3, 7, 14, 30 days); if you missed it, it comes back tomorrow.
pasos.3: Ten minutes of reviews a day are worth more than a whole night before the exam.

espaciada.porQue: What you review with gaps in between is forgotten far more slowly than what you cram all at once.

feynman.linea: Explain it as if to a 12 year old.
feynman.que: If you can't explain it in simple words, you don't understand it yet. This technique shows you where the gap is.

pasos.0: Write the concept you want to understand at the top of a sheet of paper.
pasos.1: Explain it in writing as if you were telling someone who knows nothing about the topic.
pasos.2: Where you get stuck or fall back on jargon, go back to your notes: that is the gap.
pasos.3: Simplify and use an example of your own until the explanation comes out clean.

feynman.porQue: Explaining forces you to order your ideas and exposes what you thought you knew and didn't.

flashcards.linea: Question on the front, answer on the back.
flashcards.que: Question and answer cards you review with spaced repetition (Leitner system): the ones you miss come back sooner.

pasos.1: One idea per card: definitions, formulas, dates, steps.
pasos.2: Answer from memory before you flip it and say whether it went right, so-so or wrong.
pasos.3: Review today's cards every day; you don't need more.

flashcards.porQue: It combines active recall with spacing: each card is reviewed right when it is needed.

mapas.linea: See the whole topic on one page.
mapas.que: A drawing of the topic: the central idea in the middle and branches with what hangs from it.

pasos.0: In the center of a blank sheet, the topic in two or three words.
pasos.1: Branches with the main ideas; from each one, its details.
pasos.2: Keywords, not sentences. Arrows for what connects across branches.
pasos.3: Redo it from memory when you review and compare with the original.

mapas.porQue: It orders information by relationships, and redoing it from memory is another form of active recall.

anteriores.linea: Mock exam with a real paper and a clock.
anteriores.que: Doing exams from other years under the same conditions as the real one. It is the best rehearsal there is.

pasos.0: Get exams from previous years (teacher, student reps, classmates).
pasos.1: Do it timed, no notes and no phone, as if it were the day.
pasos.2: Mark it with the answers and log each mistake by topic.
pasos.3: The topics you miss most go to reviewing and back into the plan.

anteriores.porQue: You practice the format, the time and the pressure, and you find out what really comes up.

pomodoro.que: Short blocks of total focus with fixed breaks. Every four blocks, a long break.

pasos.0: Pick a single task and put your phone on silent.
pasos.1: Focus until the bell rings; if you get distracted, go back to the task without guilt.
pasos.2: Rest for real: away from the screen.

pomodoro.porQue: An end in sight makes it easier to start and hold your attention, and the breaks keep you from burning out by the fourth block.
